To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
KPCA, 2DKPCA, 2DPCA and PCA are used to compare the performance of the algorithms in face recognition.
PCA is a simple and effective feature extraction technique, but its performance is not good enough to be used in real time applications.
KPCA is the most efficient technique among all the techniques mentioned in this paper.
In summary, our research is concerned with
comparative analysis of PCA family.
the comparison of linear and nonlinear PCA based techniques in terms of recognition performance.
the performance evaluation of PCA based methods and their comparison with respect to recognition rate and testing criteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the performance of PCA based methods depends upon the dataset used for testing.
KPCA outperforms other PCA family methods.
the K series of PCA are better than simple PCA and 02PCA in terms of recognition accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
K series of 2DPCA outperforms other PCA based techniques in terms of computational time and accuracy.
K series of 2DPCA is the most reliable technique in terms of performance and computational complexity.
the performance of PCA family depends on the dataset used for training and the testing criteria set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the PCA based techniques depends on the dataset used and the testing parameters set by the authors.
K series of 2DPCA is more suitable for face recognition than 2DPCA.
, for better performance, K series of PCA is recommended.
